manifest.name: Ops
manifest.description: Makemind Ops — per-project operations console for tasks, processes, knowledge, members, skills, profiles, philosophies, and bundles. vibe_studio built-in app: each Ops tab binds a single project directory (standard newProjectInActive / openProjectInActive wiring); members, tasks, skills, processes, philosophies, profiles, and knowledge live inside the project. The seed ships only the shared `ops.manager` agent and operations-manual knowledge that every project reuses.

sources.title: Ops — identity, project layout, surfaces
sources.description: Makemind Ops identity, project structure, sidebar, agent / lifecycle wiring. Entry point for both external LLM clients and the host chat manager.

documents.title: Ops overview — purpose + positioning
documents.content:
# Ops overview

Makemind Ops is a per-project operations console (vibe_studio built-in app `makemind_ops`) — a company-like operating environment where agents and people run work across workspaces.

## Identity
- One Ops tab = one project directory (standard host wiring, like App Builder / Scene Builder). First entry forces New / Open.
- Operations data (members · tasks · processes · skills · profiles · philosophies · knowledge) live inside the bound project. Seed = shared `ops.manager` agent + this operations manual; no operations data.

## Sidebar (14 routes, grouped)
- Overview: Home · Activity (observability)
- Experts: Experts (members)
- Knowledge: Knowledge · Skills · Profiles · Philosophies
- Work: **Inbox** (human approval + task queue) · Tasks · Processes · Workspaces
- System: Bundles · Audit · About
(Chat and Settings are host chrome — `chromeBridge.activeChatAgentId` + the domain panel in the host Settings dialog.)

## Operating model — the 3-axis matrix
Workspace (unit work-space, free granularity + formal sharing) × Org (hierarchy, approval + escalation) × Process (cross-workspace work unit; agents and people; gates, human steps, auto-chaining). People are approvers + doers via the Inbox. See the ops_concepts `matrix_model` doc.

## 5 facades + 9 host capabilities
- Knowledge facades × 5 — Facts · Skills · Profiles · Philosophies · Knowledge files.
- Host capability packs (shared `<id>.*`) — io · channel · browser · fs · db · canvas · kv · analysis · form · ingest (catalog: `studio://knowledge/studio_host_tools/capabilities`).

Runs in hybrid mode on the vibe_studio backbone (`KernelApp.system`); ensureBoot rebinds on project change.

documents.title: Ops project layout — one bound project per Ops tab
documents.content:
# Project layout

Ops uses standard vibe_studio built-in wiring — one Ops tab = one project.

## Forced entry
- Empty tab = wizard (`New project` / `Open project` two buttons).
- User selection → `chromeBridge.newProjectInActive` / `openProjectInActive` → `_bindProject` → KnowledgeInit boot.
- The seed contains only the policy layer (shared `ops.manager` + operations manual). No data (organizations · projects · members · tasks · etc.).

## Project folder layout
```
<currentProject>/                — Ops project root (selected by user via New / Open)
  project.opsproj               — marker (checked by `isOpsProjectDir`)
  _system/                      — reserved (home workspace for `ops.manager`)
  members/                      — agent · person (member.yaml)
  philosophies/                 — editorial principles etc. (yaml)
  processes/                    — multi-step workflow definitions + execution history
  profiles/                     — agent persona definitions (yaml)
  skills/                       — MCP tool definitions + action bodies (yaml)
  tasks/                        — single-shot task queue
  knowledge/                    — Fact · Pattern · Summary · files
  auth/                         — external channel credentials (Keychain · encrypted)
```

## Shared vs per-project
- **Shared (seed)** — `ops.manager` agent + operations manual (`studio://knowledge/ops_*`).
- **Per-project** — assets in the folders above. All operations data added by the user.

## Project switching
- Project Header `Open` or wizard `Open project` — select a different directory.
- `_bindProject` re-invoked → KnowledgeInit rebinds to the new root.

documents.title: Ops lifecycle wiring — chrome bridge contract
documents.content:
# Lifecycle wiring

The Ops shell follows only the standard host chrome wiring (same contract as App Builder / Scene Builder).

## chrome bridge slots
- `chromeBridge.newProjectInActive` — `_newProject({name, parent})` — creates directory + `applyOpsProjectSeed` + `_bindProject`.
- `chromeBridge.openProjectInActive` — `_openProject(path)` — validates with `isOpsProjectDir`, then `_bindProject`.
- `chromeBridge.closeProjectInActive` — `_closeProject()` — `_currentProject = null` + `resetBootCache`.
- `chromeBridge.lifecycleState` — pushes `DomainLifecycleState(hasProject, projectName)` ("No project open" on Home, `basename(dir)` when bound).

## Active-tab gate
IndexedStack eagerly mounts all tab bodies, so the chrome bridge is a process-wide singleton. If two Ops tabs are mounted simultaneously, the later one can capture the slot — all chrome bridge writes must pass the `_isActiveTab` check (`BuiltInAppRegistry.instance.activeContext?.bundlePath == widget.bundlePath`) before executing.

## Boot cache
`OpsBuiltInApp.ensureBoot({backbone, currentProject})` — process-wide cache.
- When `currentProject` changes, a new boot is triggered and the previous boot's facade is disposed.
- Same project + same backbone = cached instance returned.
- `resetBootCache` (closeProject path) registers dispose → the next ensureBoot creates a fresh KnowledgeInit.

documents.title: Ops agents — shared `ops.manager` (seed) + per-project members
documents.content:
# Agents

## What an agent IS (identity)
An agent (member) is a **persistent, individuated mind** — its own thinking, knowledge, and philosophy — that **accumulates expertise in its role over time**. It is NOT a disposable one-shot worker spun up per task and discarded: that accumulates nothing and is no different from one agent doing everything. Delegating to a member means handing work to a specific, growing expert whose competence deepens with every turn.

### Why individuated (the reason we split context)
A single LLM cannot hold and reason over all of a large, wide domain at once. So the organization splits into individuated minds, each accumulating depth at its own boundary. Distribution is not the goal — the accumulating individual intelligence is. Give a member a durable role; don't reshuffle work across anonymous runners.

### Where a member's expertise accumulates (durable substrate)
- **Owned skills** — a member forks its own skill overlays (`agent_owned_skill`) that evolve independently: personalized, sharpening competence.
- **Owned philosophy** — a member's own ethos / persona (`agent_owned_philosophy`) it carries and refines.
- **FactGraph** — experience persists as facts (invocations, forks, org lessons) in the project's `.factgraph`, surviving restarts.
- **Conversation history** — each member's turn history persists (`agent_get_history`), giving continuity across sessions.
This is where "what I have learned in this role" lives — a member builds on it, it does not start blank.

## `ops.manager` — the project coordinator (shared, seed)
`ops.manager` is the Studio's **coordinator** for the whole Ops project — the single human interface, the one channel for every work instruction. It is NOT a member of any workspace's org chart, and there is exactly **one per project** (never one per workspace). Workspaces are data-isolation lenses that all run concurrently: you never "activate a workspace to reach its manager" — you always talk to the one coordinator, which delegates across every workspace (`agent_ask` / `agent_route` / `process_start` reach members in any workspace). Switching the active workspace changes only the VIEW (which department's data + roster you see), never the coordinator or its single conversation.

- ID: `ops.manager` — registered in the seed's `manifest.agents[]`, shared across all Ops projects.
- Display: "Ops Manager"
- Role: `manager` — vibe_studio's chat routing convention routes chat entry via `role: manager`.
- Tool allowlist = explicit 83-entry list in the seed's agents block (bk.* 10 · browser.* 3 · ops domain tools 70). An empty list would fall back to the role-default catalog instead.
- Host chat = automatically routed to `ops.manager` via `chromeBridge.activeChatAgentId = 'ops.manager'` when the Ops tab is active.
- Auxiliary home workspace = the bound project's `_system/` directory (ensured at boot).

## Project members (per project)
- Defined in `members/*.yaml` within the bound project.
- type = `agent` (LLM) or `person` (external user).
- Agent members have their own LLM model, skill allowlist, and persona (profile) — and, per above, their own accumulating skills / philosophy / facts / history. Persistent individuals, not ephemeral runners.
- Separate from the seed's `ops.manager` — project members participate only in that project's operations flow (publish · review · ads · etc.), each deepening its specialty.

## Delegation calls
- Single-turn member agent call = `agent_ask({agentId:'<member_id>', message})` — one turn in that member's ongoing, accumulating history (not a fresh throwaway worker).
- Batch work for a member agent = `task_create({title, skill, args, assigneeId:'<member_id>'})` or `process_start` — assigned to that persistent member, whose expertise the work adds to.

sources.title: Ops delegation patterns — manager → member / skill / process / task
sources.description: Decision tree for how the manager (ops.manager) delegates or executes when it receives an operations request.

documents.title: Decision tree — user request → call flow
documents.content:
# Delegation decision tree

> **Who you delegate to:** members are **persistent, individuated minds** that accumulate expertise in their role (see ops_overview → Agents). "Task" / "one-shot" below name *execution mechanisms* — a unit of work — NOT the nature of the worker. Assigning work to a member adds to that member's growing competence; it does not spin up a throwaway. Prefer giving a durable member ongoing responsibility over reshuffling work across anonymous runners.

## 1. Data retrieval / status check
- Single fact → `knowledge_fact_query`. File read/list → `knowledge_file_read` / `knowledge_file_list`.
- List members / skills / processes / bundles → `member_list` / `skill_list` / `process_list` / `bundle_installed`. Config → `config_get`.

## 2. Single-action execution (a unit of work, not a disposable worker)
- Run a skill once = `task_create({skill:'<id>', args, title})` → `task_run`. Result = `task_get({id})`. When `assigneeId` is a member, this work accrues to that persistent member's expertise.
- Run a real command / file / db op = a host capability (`io.execute`, `fs.*`, `db.*`) — directly or inside a process step.

## 3. Multi-step workflow
- Defined process exists = `process_start({id})`. Else define with `process_save({yaml})` then start.
- Progress = `process_get({id})` / `process_runs({id})`.

## 4. Human in the loop (matrix)
- A gate awaiting approval → `approvals_pending({approverId?})`; approve = `process_approve({id, approverId})` (designated approver or org-ancestor).
- A human work-step → `tasks_pending({assigneeId?})`; the person completes via `step_submit`.
- Each affects only its own run — everything else keeps running.

## 5. Direct member call
- A turn with a member = `agent_ask({agentId, message})` — one turn in that member's ongoing, accumulating history (`agent_get_history`), not a fresh worker. Routing = `agent_route({intent})`.

## Priority order
**process > task > direct tool/capability call > agent_ask**. A process provides approval gates, human steps, auto-chaining, and audit. `agent_ask` is for reasoning delegation to a persistent member; simple tool/capability calls the manager makes directly. Whichever mechanism you pick, the member on the other side is a durable individual whose expertise compounds — delegate to grow it.

documents.title: Member creation / attachment flow
documents.content:
# Member flow

## New agent member
```
member_create_agent({
  id: 'editor.junior',
  displayName: 'Junior Editor',
  profileRef: '<profile_id>',
  philosophyRef: '<philosophy_id>',
  skillIds: ['content_review', 'ad_publish'],
  model: { provider: 'anthropic', model: 'claude-sonnet-4-6' }
})
```
(Param names are `profileRef` · `philosophyRef` · `skillIds` — not `profile`/`skills`.)

## Person member
`member_add_person({id, displayName, contact})` — a human teammate; can be a process step's approver (`gates.approverId`) or doer (`assigneeId` + `skillId: human`).

## Workspace attach / detach
- Pull from global pool = `member_attach({memberId})` · Remove = `member_detach({memberId})` · Global list = `member_global_list`.

## Channel credentials
`member_capture_auth({memberId, channel:'slack'|'discord'|...})` — stores token in Keychain.

documents.title: Skill definition flow
documents.content:
# Skill flow

## New skill
`skill_save({id, scope:'workspace'|'agent', body:{description, inputSchema, action}})`.

## Auto-generate
`skill_generate({goal:'...natural language goal...'})` — generates skill definition candidates via LLM. User confirms, then `skill_save`.

## 3-level scope
- **template** — provided by seed / bundle. Global: visible in every workspace.
- **workspace** — the workspace's own `skills/*.yaml` (`skill_save({scope:'workspace'})`). Scoped to that workspace **and inherited down the org tree** — a child workspace sees its parent/ancestor skills, but a sibling (or the parent) does NOT see a workspace's own skills. `skill_list` in a workspace lists only its in-scope skills, so keep a team's abilities in that team's workspace and org-standard ones at the org root.
- **agent** — per-member overlay. `skill_save({scope:'agent', agentId})`.

## Invocation
1:1 skill tool — each skill id is used directly as the tool name. `skill_list` shows the currently available ids.

## Deletion
`skill_delete({id, scope})`. Clean up agent overlays first, then delete the workspace definition.

documents.title: Process (workflow) flow
documents.content:
# Process flow

## Definition (YAML)
`process_save({yaml, workspaceId?})` — the process is a YAML string:
```yaml
id: weekly_publish
title: Weekly Publish
steps:
  - stepId: draft
    assigneeId: editor.junior     # an agent member; OR a person + skillId: human (waits for step_submit)
    skillId: content_review
    inputs: {}
    channelThreadId: deploy        # optional handoff — posts to this in-app thread after the step
gates:
  - approverId: ops.manager        # suspends the run until this approver (or an org-ancestor) approves
triggerSource: upstream_proc_id    # optional — auto-start when that process completes (event chaining)
```

## Execution
`process_start({id, inputs?})` → `{runId, state, currentStep}`. `state: waitingApproval` = paused at a gate; `waitingTask` = paused at a human step.
- Approve a gate = `process_approve({id, approverId})` — must be the designated approver or an org-ancestor (escalation).
- Resume / cancel = `process_resume` / `process_cancel`. History = `process_runs({id})` · single run = `process_get({id})`.

## Patterns (matrix model)
- Cross-workspace: a step's `assigneeId` may be an agent in another workspace — the process spans workspaces.
- Human approval = a `gate` (designated `approverId`; suspends only this run; escalates up the org tree). Human work = a `human` step (queued in `tasks_pending`, completed via `step_submit`).
- Auto-chaining = `triggerSource` (A completes → B starts unattended). Recurring = schedule/cron.

## Parallel steps (`dependsOn`)
By default each step depends on the textually-previous one (a linear chain). Give a step `dependsOn: [stepA, stepB]` to declare an explicit DAG — steps that share a predecessor (or depend on nothing) run **concurrently** (the engine schedules by topological level). Example: after `build`, run `frontend` / `art` / `video` in parallel, then `integrate` with `dependsOn: [frontend, art, video]`. Don't force a sequence when work is actually parallel. The Organization **Workflow** view renders `dependsOn` as parallel branches and `triggerSource` as an event edge between process cards.

documents.title: External channels — notify + inbound approval/action
documents.content:
# External channels (notify · inbound → approve/act)

External messaging (KakaoTalk · email · Slack · Telegram · …) composes from EXISTING primitives — no bespoke engine. You (a persistent agent) drive it.

## Connect (once, per external channel)
- `channel.connect{platform, id, params}` provisions a real connector (params = that platform's credentials, e.g. kakao `botId`, slack `botToken`, email `botEmail`). `channel.list` shows connected; `channel.disconnect{id}` stops one. `in_app` is always present.

## Inbound → who handles it (routing is data)
- `channel.bind{conversationId, agentId}` routes inbound from that conversation to an agent. The in-app feed uses conversationId == agentId; external conversations need a bind. `channel.bindings` lists them.
- An inbound message then reaches the bound agent, which DECIDES and acts with its normal tools — this is the flexible glue, not a hardcoded rule:
  - approve a waiting gate → `process_approve{processId, approved:true}` (the approval engine already exists; never reimplement it).
  - delegate work → `agent_route{managerId, request, candidateAgentIds, execute:true}`.
  - reply / report back → `channel.send{channelId, conversationId, text}`.

## Outbound notify (progress → owner)
- Send progress/results to an owner/requester with `channel.send`. Express it in a process step or as part of your flow — not as host magic. A recurring task's assignee agent can notify on completion the same way.

## Why this shape
Studio is a tool: the host exposes composable primitives (`channel.*`, `process_approve`, `agent_route`), and the wiring is DATA (bindings, process definitions) + your judgment as a persistent agent — generic and flexible, reused identically by AppPlayer / FlowBrain.

## Credentials (secure vault)
- Store an account's credentials in the OS keychain with `channel.credential_set{id, platform, params}` (params = that platform's fields — no plaintext read-back). `channel.connect{id}` then resolves them, so secrets never travel in the connect call / chat / logs. `channel.credential_ids` lists ids; `channel.credential_remove{id}` deletes. The `id` distinguishes accounts (same platform, different accounts = different ids). Inline `params` still override.

## Where an operator enters it (UI)
- **System → Channels** page: pick a platform, fill its fields, Save & connect (company / shared accounts).
- **A member's menu (Experts) → Contact channel**: bind a conversation (their room / address) to that member, so inbound routes to them and they can be reached there (person or agent).

sources.title: Ops 5 facades — knowledge / skill / profile / philosophy / fact
sources.description: The meaning and storage layout of each of Ops's 5 knowledge facades. The basis for semantic distinction when ops.manager composes delegation / retrieval flows.

documents.title: Knowledge facade — fact graph + file store
documents.content:
# Knowledge facade

Free-form knowledge for a project. Two kinds:

## 1. Fact (graph triple)
- Based on mcp_fact_graph. `knowledge_fact_save({subject, predicate, object, source})` · `knowledge_fact_query({subject?, predicate?, object?})`.
- Cross-workspace reads honor formal `workspace_share` grants (a shared scope is merged read-only, tagged with its origin).

## 2. File
- Files under the project's `knowledge/` folder. `knowledge_file_write` / `knowledge_file_read` / `knowledge_file_list({prefix})` / `knowledge_file_delete`.
- `knowledge_ingest_file({path})` — ingest an external file (chunking via the host `ingest.*` capability) into facts.
(No `knowledge_query` tool — retrieval is fact-query + file-list.)

documents.title: Skill facade — MCP tools + action bodies
documents.content:
# Skill facade

MCP tools that the project or its members can invoke. YAML definition + action body (script · prompt · tool chain).

- `skill_list` / `skill_get` / `skill_save` / `skill_delete` / `skill_generate` / `skill_global_list`.
- Scope = template (global) / workspace (own + inherited from org ancestors, isolated from siblings) / agent (see skill_lifecycle in ops_delegation).
- Invocation = skill id is the tool name as-is. Use `skill_list` output to confirm available ids.

documents.title: Profile facade — agent persona
documents.content:
# Profile facade

Persona definition for agent members (voice tone · values · operational context).

- Location = project `profiles/<id>.yaml`.
- Assigned via `profile: '<id>'` when calling `member_create_agent`.
- Multiple agents can share the same profile.
- Merged as part of the LLM system prompt.

documents.title: Philosophy facade — editorial / operational principles
documents.content:
# Philosophy facade

Editorial principles / operational values for the project — the axis an agent should follow when making decisions.

- Location = project `philosophies/<id>.yaml`.
- 4-axis structure (axis name · scale · principles · examples).
- A profile can reference a philosophy → becomes the agent's decision basis.
- Host comparison tool = `philosophy_compare` (Ops UI); agent receives it merged into systemPrompt.

documents.title: Unified index of the 5 facades
documents.content:
# Unified index

`KnowledgeInit.boot` attaches all 5 facades (Facts · Skills · Profiles · Philosophies · Knowledge files).
- Per-facade retrieval = that facade's query/list tool (`knowledge_fact_query` · `skill_list` · `member_list` · …).
- A workspace sees its own facets + any scopes granted to it via `workspace_share` (sandbox + explicit grant).
- External LLM = reads the seed manual via `studio://knowledge/ops_*` resources (host fan-out); shared host-capability catalog via `studio://knowledge/studio_host_tools/*`.

documents.title: Operating model — the 3-axis matrix
documents.content:
Ops runs a company-like operating model on three orthogonal axes; a real operation is a point in their matrix.

## 1. Workspace (unit shared work-space)
`workspace_create({type:'org'|'personal'|'project', ...})`. Granularity is free (a team, a whole company, one project). Sharing between workspaces is **formal**: a private sandbox by default, with explicit `workspace_share` grants (read-only scope) — not transitive full access. Workspaces are organizational **classifications / views** — they all run concurrently; switching the active one changes only which department is in focus (its data + roster), NOT which agents are running. The single project coordinator (`ops.manager`) spans every workspace: department isolation lives at the data layer (facts / members / skills per workspace), while the human interface stays one.

## 2. Org (hierarchy — approval + collaboration)
Workspaces nest into an org tree (`workspace_set_parent` / `workspace_tree`, parent/ancestors). A process approval gate names a `approverId`; if the caller isn't the designated approver, an **org-ancestor** can still approve (escalation).

## 3. Process (work / operation unit)
A `process_save` YAML spans steps across workspaces. Steps are agents or **people** (`skillId: human`). Gates suspend a run for human approval; human steps queue in `tasks_pending`. Processes auto-chain via `triggerSource`. Concurrent same-agent requests are serialized through a per-agent queue (no lost turns).

## People
A member can be an agent or a person; a person is an **approver** (`approvals_pending`) and/or a **doer** (`tasks_pending` → `step_submit`). A human action affects only its own run — everything else keeps running.

sources.title: Ops — organization & operations design methodology
sources.description: How to DESIGN and OPERATE a real organization/project on Ops (not just which tool does what). Use this to coach the user when they want to set up or structure an org/project. Canonical human handbook: docs/makemind_ops/ORG-DESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md.

documents.title: When & how to apply org design
documents.content:
# Designing an organization on Ops

When the user wants to *build or operate* an organization/project (not just run one feature), don't just call a tool — help them design it. Three goals frame every decision:
- **Delegation** — repetitive/structured work to agents; judgment/approval to people.
- **Audit** — the more important the work, the more it must leave a trace. Prefer process over ad-hoc chat, approval gates over silent automation.
- **Growth** — agents evolve their own skills/profile/philosophy/facts (4-axis fork) with use.

Governing principle: **automate where possible, but put a gate on anything irreversible or outbound.**

Design order: (1) workspaces (where work/data lives) -> (2) members & agent roles (who) -> (3) delegation ladder per task (how it flows) -> (4) knowledge & audit (what to keep). Two coordinate systems: the **3-axis** org model (Workspace x Org hierarchy x Process) and the **4-axis** agent (skill, profile, philosophy, facts).

documents.title: Workspace modeling — cutting the org
documents.content:
# Workspace modeling

A workspace is the **isolation boundary + knowledge boundary + approval unit**. Cut it first; it is the hardest decision to undo.

Type choice:
- `project/<slug>` — a single independent effort. Flat, no hierarchy. Best default starting point.
- `org/<slug>` — multiple people/functions needing an approval line. Build a tree with `workspace_set_parent`; approvals escalate to ancestors.
- `personal/<slug>` — solo.

Rule: **sharing boundary == workspace boundary.** A workspace's facts are private by default; another workspace reads them only via an explicit, read-only, scoped `workspace_share(to, scope)` (not transitive). So: "I want to wall this data off" is the signal to make a new workspace; if you'd share it freely, keep them together.

Org hierarchy is an approval/structure overlay, not nested folders — data stays isolated per workspace; only the approval chain (via `workspace_tree`) crosses.

Anti-patterns: one giant workspace mixing unrelated teams (knowledge bleeds, no control); over-splitting one person's work into many workspaces (share-grant churn). If sharing is constant, merge.

## Unit lead (팀장)
Set a workspace's head: `workspace_set_lead({id, memberId})`. The lead is the apex of the unit in the Organization chart (Structure lens) — members report to it — and the natural default approver / escalation target. A workspace IS the org unit at any scale (team / dept / company); nest workspaces (`workspace_set_parent`) to compose teams into larger units. There is NO separate Team entity — recursion is the team model.

## 사상·지식은 org 라인 따라 상속 (07 §182)
Charter(사상)와 knowledge는 워크스페이스의 **자기 ancestor 체인**(parentId 라인, 같은 라인만 — 형제/다른 브랜치 절대 아님)을 따라 상속된다:
- **charter**: prohibitions 는 라인 따라 **누적**(회사 ∘ 부서 ∘ 자기 — 다 gate). mission/northStar/values 는 **최근접**(자기 것 있으면 자기, 없으면 가장 가까운 상위). `workspace_get_charter` 는 이 유효 charter + `inheritedFrom` 반환, `philosophy_check` 게이트는 체인 전체 prohibitions 강제.
- **knowledge**: `knowledge_file_list`/`knowledge_file_read` 가 자기 것 + 상위 `knowledge/` 를 상속(자기 파일이 상위 동명 shadow, `inheritedFrom` 표시).
감사팀이 실행부서(옆 라인) 사상을 물려받지 않도록 — 상속은 오직 자기 조상 체인.

documents.title: Member & agent role design
documents.content:
# Members & agent roles

- **Person** = approver/doer of human steps (`email` + informational `roleLabels`). Real authority comes from being a gate's designated approver, not from a label.
- **Agent** = autonomous worker with its own LLM + 4-axis fork.

Default shape: **manager-worker.** `ops.manager` (shared, full toolkit) routes; user-defined worker agents do one narrow role each with minimal skills/permissions. Do not pile all skills onto one super-agent — one agent per role keeps evolution, audit, and model choice clean.

Model per agent (`ModelSpec`): big model (e.g. claude-opus-4-8) for reasoning/review/complex writing; small model (e.g. claude-haiku-4-5) for simple/high-volume. Mixing per role is optimal.

Authority = gates, NOT RBAC (there is no fine-grained role permission system):
1. **approval gate** — designated approver before risky/outbound steps.
2. **philosophy gate** — agent-level hard prohibition; violating step is blocked.
3. **share contract** — `workspace_share` scope bounds knowledge exposure.

External-system credentials: capture once via `browser.open_login` (headful) -> `auth_capture` -> `member_capture_auth`; store secrets in the `secret.*` vault, never in facts.

Unit lead (팀장 / `workspace_set_lead`) is distinct from a gate approver: an approver is per-step authority, the lead is the unit's standing head — the top of the Organization-chart hierarchy and the default approver / escalation target when work is owned by the unit.

## Role = Profile (persona)
The functional role (기자 / 편집자 / 디자이너 …) IS the **Profile** — the persona axis (voice · values · operational context), pooled at the project level and inherited by workspaces. Assigning a member a profile assigns their role; the workspace profile pool is the role catalog. The org chart's Structure lens shows each member's role FROM their profile.

Orthogonal to persona is the **orchestration role** `worker | manager | reviewer` (`AgentRole` — manager routes, reviewer verdicts). Set it with `member_create_agent({role})`; omit and it inherits the assigned profile's `defaultRole` (a profile YAML may declare `defaultRole: manager`), else worker. So: profile = who they are (persona/role); AgentRole = how they act in handoffs.

documents.title: Delegation ladder — making work flow
documents.content:
# Delegation ladder

Always pick the **lightest adequate** rung; climb only when needed:

`direct tool call` -> `task` -> `process` -> `agent_ask`

- Simple query/change -> call the tool directly.
- Run one defined skill once -> `task` (`task_create` -> `task_run`). Kinds: oneOff / recurring (cron) / sustained.
- Multi-step, multiple actors, approval or audit needed -> `process` (`process_save` YAML -> `process_start`).
- Delegate reasoning/review -> `agent_ask({agentId})`.

The one question that splits **task vs process**: *"Does a human approve mid-way, or must it leave a trace?"* No -> task. Yes -> process. Anything irreversible or sent to an external system (publishing, payments, messages) goes through a gated process, never a bare task or chat.

Within a process, declare step `dependsOn` so independent steps run in parallel rather than forcing a sequence — match the real shape of the work.

documents.title: Process, skills, knowledge — the operating fabric
documents.content:
# Process, skills, knowledge

**Process** is the audit-first primitive; the behavior engine owns durable suspend/resume. A process = ordered `steps` (each: stepId, assigneeId, skillId, inputs) + `gates` + a `trigger`. Gate kinds: `philosophy` (hard rule), `quality` (LLM appraisal), `approval` (suspends until the designated approver, or an org ancestor, calls `process_approve`). Human steps (assignee is a person / skillId human) wait for `step_submit`. Automate chains with `triggerSource`: process B auto-starts when process A completes. Split long flows into small processes chained this way.

**Skills** resolve in 3 layers: agent overlay (members/<agent>/skills) > workspace (skills/, the workspace's own plus any inherited down the org ancestor chain) > template/bundle (global). A workspace's own skills stay scoped to it and its org descendants — a sibling unit does not see them (team-capability isolation), while a child inherits its parent's. Same skillId can differ per agent, so personalization/evolution never breaks others. Org-standard ability -> workspace scope (author at the org root to share it downward); an agent's variant -> agent scope (`skill_save scope=agent`). Well-evolved skills transfer via `agent_assign_skill`.

**Knowledge**: FactGraph (semantic, queried with shared facts merged) + KV facts (`knowledge_fact_save`). External systems are taught as schema under knowledge/systems/<id>/ (url-map, extraction, auth-spec). Keep sharing an explicit scoped contract, never "everything open".

**Portability**: move a whole org with `opspack_export`/`import`; migrate creds with `credentials_export`/`import`; reusable org templates ship as bundles (`bundle_install`).

documents.title: Setup scenarios & checklist
documents.content:
# Setup scenarios + checklist

**Solo operator** — one `personal/me`; 2-3 worker agents (researcher=small model, writer/reviewer=big); routine reads via direct call / recurring task; outbound work via process + approval (approver = the user); capture external logins once.

**10-person team lead** — `org/team` root + functional children via `workspace_set_parent`; people as person members, one agent per function; core flows as processes with human review steps + approval escalating to the parent org; policy lives in `org/team` facts shared down with `workspace_share(scope: policy)`; chain flows with `triggerSource`.

**Publishing org (audit-centric)** — draft via task (fast), but formal publish only as a gated process: draft(editor) -> review(reviewer) -> philosophy gate -> approval gate -> publish(browser.submit_form) -> record fact -> auto-trigger metrics process. Never publish from ad-hoc chat.

**Design checklist**: workspaces cut on isolation/sharing boundary? org tree + approval line actually wired? one agent per role, minimal scope, right model? lightest adequate delegation rung chosen? gates on irreversible/outbound work? external systems as knowledge schema + secrets in vault? sharing explicit scoped contracts? unattended flows chained via triggerSource?

documents.title: Organization chart — 3 lenses over the same data
documents.content:
# Organization chart

The Ops **Organization** route renders the org three ways over the same registry data (a lens switch — no single view shows everything):

- **Workflow** — processes as event-topology: each process a unit card (trigger badge manual/event/task), connected by event edges (`triggerSource`); inside a card, steps lay out by their `dependsOn` DAG so independent steps stack as parallel branches; approval gates show a sign-off marker above the gated step, philosophy/quality gates as an inline charter checkpoint.
- **Structure** — the org chart: each workspace (org unit) is a framing box; its lead (팀장, `leadMemberId`) sits on top with reporting lines to members; nested workspaces compose sub-teams into larger units. Members carry an agent / human marker.
- **Knowledge** — members linked to the skill / profile / philosophy they reference.

Implication for design: author `leadMemberId` (unit head), step `dependsOn` (parallel), and `triggerSource` (event chaining) and the chart reflects the real org — hierarchy, parallel work, and event coordination — automatically. A flat single linear process is usually a modeling smell.

sources.title: Ops browser primitive recipes (9 ops)
sources.description: Usage patterns for the 9 host browser tools (browser.page_view · browser.web_search · browser.extract · browser.crawl · browser.monitor · browser.submit_form · browser.download · browser.page_audit_role · browser.page_compare_actors).

documents.title: Meaning of the 9 primitives
documents.content:
# 9 browser primitives

| name | purpose |
|---|---|
| `browser.page_view` | Render a URL page + capture DOM (commonly the first step in a skill). |
| `browser.web_search` | Search engine query. |
| `browser.extract` | Page + selector → structured data. |
| `browser.crawl` | Page + depth → URL tree. |
| `browser.monitor` | URL diff watcher. |
| `browser.submit_form` | Form input / submission (auth · CRUD). |
| `browser.download` | File / media download. |
| `browser.page_audit_role` | Compare a page from a role perspective (UX QA). |
| `browser.page_compare_actors` | Diff the same page across two actors (permission / persona QA). |

All run on the host's shared `browser.*` capability (one mcp_browser engine, owned by the host — built-ins use it, never their own).

documents.title: Research + reporting pattern
documents.content:
# Research flow

```
browser.web_search({query})   // collect candidate URLs
  ↓
browser.page_view({url})      // capture page body
  ↓
browser.extract({url, selector})  // structure the data
  ↓
knowledge_save({...}) /
knowledge_fact_save / knowledge_file_write    // persist to facade
  ↓
skill 'research_and_report'   // generate report (recommended inside a process)
```

documents.title: Publish / channel flow
documents.content:
# Publish flow

```
browser.submit_form({url, fields})  // CMS login or post creation
  ↓
browser.download({url, savePath})   // retrieve attachments or assets
  ↓
channel_notify({channelId, payload})  // Slack / Discord notification
```

The skill `ad_publish` wraps this flow. When defined as a multi-step process, a human approval step can be inserted.

sources.title: Ops tool catalog — actual tool surface on the host endpoint
sources.description: The tool surface visible to ops.manager and external LLM clients — tools registered by McpInbound.registerToolsOn plus 1:1 skill tools.

documents.title: config_*
documents.content:
- `config_get` — full OpsConfig JSON (workspacesRoot · activeWorkspace · llm · mcp · ...).
- `config_reload` — re-reads `~/.makemind-ops/config.yaml`.
- `config_set_llm_provider` · `config_set_mcp_outbound` · `config_set_storage` · `config_set_chromium` — partial updates.
- `system_agent_set_model` — routes a ModelSpec to whichever registry owns the target agent (default `_ops_admin`, a custom per-project system agent, or a workspace-scoped chat manager `ops.manager.<unit>` on the shared host).

documents.title: workspace_*
documents.content:
- `workspace_list` — workspaces in the current project.
- `workspace_create({type:'org'|'personal'|'project', slug, title?, projectRoot?})` · `workspace_update` · `workspace_rename` · `workspace_delete` · `workspace_switch({slug})`.
- org hierarchy (matrix axis 2): `workspace_set_parent({slug, parentId})` · `workspace_tree` — nest workspaces into an org tree (parent / ancestors); a process approval gate can escalate up this tree.
- formal sharing (matrix — sandbox + explicit grant): `workspace_share({fromWorkspaceId, toWorkspaceId, scope})` · `workspace_shares` — grant a read-only knowledge scope from one workspace to another. No grant = no cross-workspace read.

- `workspace_set_lead({id, memberId})` — set / clear the org unit's lead (팀장 / unit head); apex of the Organization-chart hierarchy + default approver/escalation target. Empty/omitted memberId clears.

documents.title: member_*
documents.content:
- `member_list` — members of the current workspace.
- `member_global_list` — global pool across all projects.
- `member_get({id})` · `member_create_agent({...})` · `member_add_person({...})` · `member_update` · `member_delete`.
- `member_attach({memberId})` · `member_detach({memberId})`.
- `member_capture_auth({memberId, channel})`.

- `member_create_agent` accepts `role` (worker | manager | reviewer) — the orchestration role. Omit to inherit the assigned profile's `defaultRole` (profile = the persona/role), else worker. Runtime-created agents are no longer forced to worker.

- `member_update` accepts `role` (worker | manager | reviewer) — re-role IN PLACE: the kernel agent record is updated (flowbrain `updateAgent(role:)`), never delete+recreate, so the individual's FactGraph · owned forks · history are preserved. The role persists in the member yaml and survives a `.kv` rebuild (boot mirror seeds from it). Unknown role values are rejected.

- `workspace_get_charter` = 자기 ancestor 체인의 **유효** charter(prohibitions 누적 + mission 최근접, `inheritedFrom` 포함). `philosophy_check` 게이트도 체인 전체 prohibitions 강제. `knowledge_file_list`/`read` = 자기+상위 knowledge 상속(`inheritedFrom`, `ownOnly` 로 자기만).

- 자율 오케스트레이션: `agent_route({managerId, request, candidateAgentIds, execute})` = 팀장/매니저가 적임 팀원에 업무분장(bare id 해소됨). `execute:true` → 그 팀원을 실제 구동해 `deliverable` 반환(분장+산출물). `task_run` = assignee가 에이전트면 그 에이전트를 실제 구동해 산출(`summary`), person/unknown이면 skill dispatch 폴백. recurring 스케줄러도 동일 경로로 담당자 구동.

documents.title: task_* + process_*
documents.content:
- task: `task_list({state?})` · `task_get({id})` · `task_create({title, skill, args, assigneeId?})` · `task_update` · `task_run({id})` · `task_cancel` · `task_delete` · `task_runs`.
- process: `process_list` · `process_get({id})` · `process_save({yaml, workspaceId?})` (YAML definition — shape in ops_delegation) · `process_start({id, inputs?})` · `process_approve({id, approverId})` · `process_resume` · `process_cancel` · `process_delete` · `process_runs({id})`.
- human inbox (matrix — people as approver + doer): `approvals_pending({approverId?})` (gates awaiting a designated approver, incl. org-ancestor escalation) · `tasks_pending({assigneeId?})` (human work-steps awaiting a person) · `step_submit({processId, stepId, result})` (a person completes their step, resuming the run).

- process steps support `dependsOn: [stepId, …]` (parallel DAG; absent = linear chain). `trigger: event` + `triggerSource: <processId>` auto-chains one process to another (event topology).

documents.title: knowledge_* + skill_* + bundle_*
documents.content:
- knowledge: `knowledge_fact_save` · `knowledge_fact_query` · `knowledge_file_write` · `knowledge_file_read` · `knowledge_file_list` · `knowledge_file_delete` · `knowledge_ingest_file`. (There is no `knowledge_query`/`knowledge_save` tool — use the fact / file tools.)
- skill: `skill_list` · `skill_get` · `skill_global_list` · `skill_save` · `skill_delete` · `skill_generate`. Plus 1:1 tools named after each registered skill id.
- bundle: `bundle_list` · `bundle_installed` · `bundle_install` · `bundle_uninstall`. opspack: `opspack_export({workspaceId, outputPath, includeFacts?, includeSecrets?, passphrase?})` · `opspack_import({packPath, conflictPolicy?, passphrase?})` — with `includeSecrets:true`+`passphrase` the pack carries the active workspace's passphrase-sealed asset credentials (see the asset / credential doc).
- reporting: `status_snapshot` · `diagnostic_export` · `html_report_export`. channel: `channel_notify` (routes through the host `channel.*` capability).
- host capability packs (shared `<id>.*`, not Ops-registered — full catalog at `studio://knowledge/studio_host_tools/capabilities`): `io.*` (sandboxed git/dart/flutter/pub exec) · `channel.*` · `browser.*` · `fs.*`/`db.*` (datastore) · `canvas.*` · `kv.*` · `analysis.*` · `form.*` · `ingest.*`. Process steps drive real work (run commands, read/write files, query a db) through these.

documents.title: agent_* + 9 browser primitives
documents.content:
- agent: `agent_ask({agentId, message})` · `agent_assign_skill` · `agent_get_history` · `agent_route({intent})`.
- browser (9, host capability): `browser.page_view` · `browser.page_audit_role` · `browser.web_search` · `browser.extract` · `browser.crawl` · `browser.monitor` · `browser.submit_form` · `browser.download` · `browser.page_compare_actors`.

Additional: ui_* (debug surface), makemind-ops:// resources (external MCP guide / concepts / workflows / tool-catalog / live-state) and prompts (getting_started · drive_workspace · author_skill · evolve_agent · compose_process).

documents.title: Resources — assets · secret.* vault · credential migration
documents.content:
Operational assets (DB · files · code · repos · homepages · deploy targets · API/MCP — internal or external alike; location is just an attribute) are managed in the Ops **Resources** route. Canon: `specs/platform/14-asset-credentials.md`.

- **register** (no schema change — a convention over knowledge facts): `knowledge_fact_save({category:"asset", key:<assetId>, value:<title>, metadata:{kind, location, locator, capability?, credentialRef?}})`. `kind`=db|file|code|repo|data|homepage|deploy|api|mcp · `location`=local|embedded|external · `locator`=path|dsn|url|bundle://|git@ · `capability`=db|fs|io|browser|mcp (how to operate it) · `credentialRef`=vault key (the secret body is NEVER in the fact). Query with `knowledge_fact_query` (category `asset`).
- **operate**: `asset_open({assetId})` — dispatches through the asset's `capability` (`fs.read` / `db.query` / `browser.page_view` / an authenticated HTTP GET), resolving `credentialRef` from the keychain INTERNALLY. Returns the result + `credentialUsed`; the secret is never returned.
- **credential vault** (`secret.*` host capability, OS keychain ns `appplayer.credentials`): `secret.set({ref,value})` · `secret.exists({ref})` · `secret.remove({ref})` · `secret.list({prefix?})`. **No plaintext `get`.** An asset holds only the `credentialRef`.
- **migrate to another machine**: `credentials_export({passphrase})` seals this workspace's asset credentials (the `credentialRef`s) under a passphrase into an opaque blob (PBKDF2→AEAD; the keychain key never leaves the device); `credentials_import({passphrase, sealed})` restores them on the target machine. A wrong passphrase restores nothing. `.opspack` export/import carry the same sealed blob via `includeSecrets`. Secrets are never echoed in plaintext either way.

documents.title: Channel tools (channel.*)
documents.content:
# Channel tools (`channel.*`) — external messaging

Host-level capability (all bundle apps). Backed by `mcp_channel` connectors + the `channel_drivers` recipe.

- `channel.list` / `channel.status{channelId}` — connected channels.
- `channel.send{channelId, conversationId, text}` — outbound (notify / reply).
- `channel.receive{...}` — inbound → routed to the bound agent (in-app: conversationId==agentId; external: via `channel.bind`).
- `channel.connect{platform, id, params?}` / `channel.disconnect{id}` — provision an external connector (slack / telegram / email / kakao). Omit `params` to resolve stored credentials by id.
- `channel.credential_set{id, platform, params}` / `credential_ids` / `credential_remove{id}` — secure vault (OS keychain, no plaintext read-back).
- `channel.bind{conversationId, agentId}` / `unbind{conversationId}` / `bindings` — route an external conversation to an agent (persisted per project).

Glue = composition, not a hardcoded engine: inbound → the agent decides (`process_approve` to approve a gate, `agent_route` to delegate, `channel.send` to reply/notify). See `ops_delegation/external_channels`. UI: System → Channels; a member's menu → Contact channel.

sources.title: Ops operating playbook — build & run any organization (field experience)
sources.description: Experience knowledge (the HOW) layered on the tool manual (the WHAT): how a fresh coordinator / external LLM builds and continuously runs a real organization of any kind. Universal core; domain- and country-specific practice is a separate, replaceable layer.

documents.title: How to use this playbook + layering
documents.content:
# How to use this playbook

This is **experience knowledge (the HOW)** — how to build and continuously run a real organization of any kind (company, magazine newsroom, church, school / academy, research lab, shop). It sits on top of the tool **manual (the WHAT)** in the other `ops_*` knowledge: the manual says which tools exist; this says how to run an organization with them. A fresh, context-free session (a chat coordinator or an external LLM) should be able to read this alone and stand up and run an organization.

**Layering.** This playbook is the **universal core**. Domain- and country-specific practice (industry regulations, tax law, local customs) is NOT here — seed it as a **separate, replaceable layer** in the organization's own `knowledge/` (see "Doctrine & knowledge layers"), so the core stays universal and the local layer swaps per country / industry.

> Source: a frozen snapshot of field experience building, operating, and verifying a real organization (13 units / 56 members) in Ops. Every pitfall and tip below is field-measured.

documents.title: Doctrine — why it works this way
documents.content:
# Doctrine — why it works this way

- **Ops is an organization's operating OS.** Org units (workspaces), members, work (process / task), knowledge, and approvals all run in one place. When it runs well, that IS the organization's operation.
- **An agent is a persistent, individuated, accumulating mind** — not a disposable worker spun up when busy and discarded. A throwaway accumulates nothing, which is no better than one agent doing everything. Design each as a named individual that lives long and deepens the expertise of its role. Why we split context: a single LLM cannot hold and reason over a large, wide domain at once — each individual accumulates bounded depth.
- **Org design only stands on domain knowledge.** Every medium has its own editorial voice; every church, academy, and company has its own operating culture and approval customs. Before creating workspaces / agents, secure *how the organization actually runs* (its operating doctrine: identity, discipline, deliverables, handoffs, gates) — ask the owner if needed. An org chart without domain knowledge is an empty box.
- **Unified purpose, diverse expression.** The charter (org doctrine) moves everyone in the same direction; each member's persona (philosophy) gives its own lens and voice. Given the same topic, they see and tell it differently — that combination is what makes agents alive.
- **People decide.** The organization produces options, rationale, even a recommended option; the decision / approval is escalated to a person (owner / lead) gate.

documents.title: Build sequence (verified)
documents.content:
# Build sequence (verified)

1. **Operating doctrine first.** Write the org's identity, discipline, deliverable model, handoffs, and gates. (A newsroom: editorial voice, review loop, publish gate. An academy: teaching, counseling, parent-reporting flow. A church: worship, pastoral care, finance procedure.) **Scale the ask to the request (do not skip doctrine silently):** for a substantial org, put the doctrine questions to the founder first; for a small or one-line request, do NOT interrogate — STATE your doctrine assumptions explicitly ("I'll assume: privacy-first, approval before any mass-send, weekly cadence") and ask for a one-word confirm, then build. The failure mode is jumping straight to structure with no stated assumptions at all.
2. **Build the top (the org's apex) first, then downward.** Put a person (lead = approval apex) and a minimal staff in the root workspace. Reason: charter, knowledge, and skills **inherit down the tree, top → bottom** — the top must stand before the bottom can inherit its identity. The approval-escalation path is the ancestor chain too.
3. **Departments / teams are children via `workspace_create` + `workspace_set_parent`.** A workspace is both an org unit and a dashboard classification lens. **"Active" has no execution meaning** — every department is always running; target tool calls with an explicit `workspaceId` (relying on a global "active" makes concurrent work step on itself). The chat is a single per-project coordinator, not one manager per workspace.
4. **Verify small → connect → expand.** Don't build big at once. Create one department, confirm it works (read / write / execute); then the next; then confirm cross-department connection (order → delivery).
5. Department-complete = 5 elements: org design (roster) · operating doctrine · workflow (process / heartbeat) · assets / resources · knowledge seed.

documents.title: Member design — the persistent roster
documents.content:
# Member design — the persistent roster

- `member_create_agent({id, displayName, role, provider, model, skillIds, profileRef, philosophyRef})`. **displayName = "Name · Role"** (e.g. "Leo · Engineering", "Grace · Copy-edit") — the name gives the individual its identity and signature. This is mandatory, not role-only: NEVER ship an agent named by its function alone ("Note-keeper", "Meeting-lead") — always a real personal name + role ("Nora · Note-keeper", "Owen · Meeting-lead"). A nameless role reads as a disposable worker, the anti-pattern; this roster is a persistent, individuated cast.
- **role**: `worker` (does the work) · `manager` (assigns / routes — the subject of `agent_route`) · `reviewer` (reviews / adjudicates). A department head = manager + `workspace_set_lead`.
- **The 4 axes are both identity and growth channels**: skill (ability) · profile (role / tone) · philosophy (ethos / persona) · facts (knowledge). Design all four.
- **philosophy = the persona model.** Don't stop at a couple of prohibition rules — fill the Ethos fully: `valuePriorities` (value ordering) · `prohibitions` (absolute moral boundaries, hard / soft) · `judgmentCriteria` (situational judgment: in this case, do this) · `directionalAttitudes` (fundamental stance toward uncertainty / failure / conflict + behavioral implications). As a person's character, philosophy, and morality govern their words and acts — given the same facts, a different persona sees and writes differently. That is the intent.
- **Re-role / rename via `member_update`** (never destroy the individual — history, forks, and expertise are preserved). Deletion is only for verification scaffolding.
- **People / external labor are person members** (`member_add_person`) — the owner, physical work (assembly, construction, shooting), outside experts (accountant, lawyer, instructor). Put them into workflows as the subject of approval gates / physical steps.
- Model tier: judgment-heavy roles (department head, planning, writing, engineering) = a higher model; mechanical execution (translation, capture, cleanup) = lightweight. With no LLM key, provider `anthropic` runs via the Claude Code fallback.

documents.title: Doctrine & knowledge layers (tree inheritance)
documents.content:
# Doctrine & knowledge layers (tree inheritance)

- **charter = org doctrine** (`workspace_set_charter`: mission · values · prohibitions · doctrineRef · northStar). Members inherit it, and a process's philosophy gate adjudicates against it.
- **Inheritance is inclusive (accumulating)**: a child department's effective doctrine = its own charter ⊕ parent ⊕ apex (all overlaid). Siblings are isolated. **Give every department its own doctrine** — the higher doctrine ("serve the organization") is shared, but the lower must differ: if an execution department (speed, shipping) and an audit / verification department (independence, skepticism) share the same doctrine, the check-and-balance dies.
- **Knowledge and skills follow the same tree rule**: org-common knowledge goes once into the apex workspace's `knowledge/` — children read it without copying. Department-specific knowledge lives in the department. (On a filename clash, the department's wins.)
- **Seed domain practice knowledge** — tax / accounting guidance, industry regulations, local (country / region) customs, etc. are a knowledge layer the org needs to work. Split what differs by country (tax law, etc.) into a local layer so it stays replaceable.
- Org-level memory: `workspace_record_lesson` (an org lesson — learning that stays with the organization even as members change).

documents.title: Workflow
documents.content:
# Workflow

- **process = artifact-unit workflow** (`process_save` YAML → `process_start`). Express **parallelism** with `dependsOn` on steps (e.g. after production, manuscript / shooting / illustration run concurrently, with layout as the join point). gates: `approval` (approverId = a person) · `philosophy` (charter adjudication). Assign human steps to person members. Pending approvals = `approvals_pending`; passing = `process_approve`.
- **task = work unit**: `recurring` + cron = a **heartbeat** (morning report, weekly wrap-up, monthly-close review — the org's pulse); `oneOff` (a single request); `sustained` (standing). `task_run` actually drives the assignee agent and leaves a summary.
- **A recurring need becomes a heartbeat, not a manual process.** When the request says "every week / daily / each morning / monthly" (e.g. "prepare the weekly meeting"), CREATE a `recurring` task with a cron — do not leave it as a manual process the operator must trigger by hand. The recurrence IS the requirement; encode it so the org's pulse runs on its own.
- **Put review / rejection loop-backs into the workflow** — quality comes from a loop, not a single gate (write ↔ review, produce ↔ verify).
- **If the org has budget / spend**: budget by **line item** (materials, outsourcing, meetings…) not a lump sum → approve → track execution → settle. Separate direct (productive) from indirect (operational) purchases, splitting owner / account. Uncertain judgments like filing / legal go to an outside expert (person) gate.

documents.title: Operating patterns (field-verified)
documents.content:
# Operating patterns (field-verified)

- **Assignment (head → member)**: `agent_route({managerId, request, candidateAgentIds, execute:true})` — reads the content, picks the right person, actually performs it, and collects the deliverable. Express expertise differences in profile and the router reflects them (complex → senior, simple → junior). For load / schedule judgment, put availability context into the request and it weighs the trade-off (urgent → whoever's free, quality-first → wait for the expert).
- **Cross-team collaboration**: an order (written by the requesting department) → the performing department's lead assigns → output → delivery (shared asset) → reschedule on a rework request. Share members across teams with `member_attach`; share a fact contract with `workspace_share`.
- **HR**: hiring = create a new persistent individual + **OJT** (inject the 4 axes: standard skills + role profile + philosophy [charter auto-inherited + specialization] + onboarding facts) — a new member aligned to the org culture. **HRD** = performance review (from history / output) → a 4-axis improvement plan → **report & approval** → apply → re-review. Never change an individual without approval.
- **Two growth loops**: (1) continuity — conversation history persists per-agent, so the individual remembers its past (automatic). (2) distillation — periodically condense its own history into distilled knowledge (expertise facts) ("compress only the reproducible know-how from your experience and store it") — expertise accumulates without context bloat.
- **Model "smarts" like scheduling / staffing judgment as org skills, not platform features** (e.g. an HR skill that observes load and proposes hiring).

documents.title: Pitfalls & tips (all field-measured)
documents.content:
# Pitfalls & tips (all field-measured)

- A long `agent_route` request (≳ 1KB) breaks routing parsing → **keep the assignment request to a one-line summary**, put detail in the performing step (`agent_ask`).
- Don't trust an agent's self-report — **verify by side effect**: did the file actually appear, did the target agent's history gain a turn.
- Recording (Scene Builder): static scenes collapse video length via duplicate-frame drop → design an interaction / settleMs per scene. Overlay captions / watermarks are not composited into capture frames → deliver captions as a separate SRT.
- `knowledge_fact_save` stores into the execution scope (the calling agent's home workspace) by default — to attribute a fact to the department it is ABOUT, pass an explicit `workspaceId`.
- Put "don't invent what isn't possible — report exactly" into agent instructions — an honest deviation-reporting culture even surfaces tool limits.
- When verifying, first check whether the process restarted (PID / start time) — it's easy to look at an old instance and misjudge it as "not fixed".

documents.title: Verification culture & healthy signals
documents.content:
# Verification culture & healthy signals

## Verification culture
- **QA is independent reproduction** — regardless of the author's report, run it yourself from scratch and adjudicate (pass / reject / hold). A rejection carries reproduction evidence and resubmission conditions. It's only real if it also catches a defect the operator planted.
- **Test against known answers** — give a task whose answer is known to tell real execution from hallucination.
- **An owner-decision queue** — collect decision items the org surfaces while operating (price, policy, regulation interpretation…) with options and escalate to a person. The organization does not decide.

## Signs the organization is running well
- The morning report comes out with real data, and the org surfaces its own issues / decision items.
- Against forbidden temptations (confirm this number, execute without approval, exaggerate the copy), it produces **refusal + rationale + a practical alternative**.
- The reject → rework → re-adjudicate loop runs without human intervention.
- The same brief yields a different lens / voice per individual, yet all stay inside the factual boundary.

agents.name: Ops Manager
agents.systemPrompt:
You are the manager for Makemind Ops — a vibe_studio built-in app for project operations. The user talks to you whenever the Ops tab is active. You speak the user's language (Korean if they write in Korean).

Identity:
  • One Ops tab = one project directory. All operational data (members / tasks / skills / processes / profiles / philosophies / knowledge) lives inside that project.
  • Seed assets = you (`ops.manager`) + the operations manual (`studio://knowledge/ops_overview/*` · `ops_delegation/*` · `ops_concepts/*` · `ops_browser_recipes/*` · `ops_tool_catalog/*`).
  • Project members (per-project agents) are separate from you — each has its own LLM, skill whitelist, and persona.

When a project is NOT bound:
  • Guide the user to the wizard's `New project` / `Open project`. The Ops wizard routes through the host chrome bridge slot.
  • Do not try to create a directory yourself — the host chrome's standard wiring handles it.

When a project IS bound — routing rules:
  1. Assess state first — the first action is `config_get` plus the needed `member_list` / `skill_list` / `process_list` / `bundle_installed`.
  2. Simple query / change → call the tool directly (you have authority over the entire Ops tool surface).
  3. Multi-step operations → if a defined process exists, prefer `process_start`. Otherwise define it with `process_save`, then `process_start`.
  4. One-off skill execution → `task_create({skill, args})` → `task_run`.
  5. Delegate reasoning / review to a member → `agent_ask({agentId:'<member_id>', message})`. For free-form intent → recommend candidates with `agent_route`.
  6. Web research → 9 host browser primitives (`browser.page_view` · `browser.web_search` · `browser.extract` · ...) → save with `knowledge_save` when needed.
  6.5 Asset / credential management (Resources route) → register operational assets with `knowledge_fact_save({category:"asset", metadata:{kind, location, locator, capability?, credentialRef?}})`; operate an asset with `asset_open`; manage secrets with the `secret.*` vault (no plaintext get); migrate credentials to another machine with `credentials_export`/`credentials_import` (or opspack `includeSecrets`). Canon: `specs/platform/14-asset-credentials.md`.
  7. Do not guess identifiers — confirm any unknown `id` with a list tool first.

Cross-builtin:
  • Other tools on the vibe_studio host endpoint (`studio.*` · `app_builder.*` · `scene.*` · `bk.*`) are exposed on the same surface. Call them only when truly needed, and prioritize your own domain (Ops).
  • The host manager (`studio.manager`) is responsible for routing other built-ins. When the user makes a request like "I want to build an app", guide them to the host manager / app_builder.

Writing:
  • Answer in markdown. For tool results, attach a one-line summary the user can act on plus only the raw output that's needed.
  • If ambiguous, ask once and proceed (especially for destructive actions: delete · cancel · uninstall).
